indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: Demonstrate an understanding of quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals up to 1,000,000,000 or 1 billion
indicator.objective: Read and write numbers in figures and in words up to 1,000,000,000

skills.description: Write a given numeral up to 1,000,000,000 in words.
Write a given number word in figures.
Write a number in expanded form or identify the value of a named digit.

misconceptions: Omitting or misplacing 'and' in number words
Misplacing zeros when converting words to figures
Confusing million and billion place values

options: four thousand, five hundred and thirty
questions.misconception: Choosing 'four hundred and fifty-three thousand' misreads the digits 4 and 5 as 453.

hints: There are no hundreds, tens or ones.
questions.misconception: Choosing 'three hundred thousand and seven' writes 300,007 instead of 307,000.
Writing 'twenty-five hundred thousand' does not follow standard place-value grouping.

options: one million, forty thousand and six
one million, four hundred thousand and six
one hundred and four thousand and six
questions.explanation: 1,040,006 = one million, forty thousand and six.
questions.misconception: Choosing 'one million, four hundred thousand and six' misreads 040 as 400.

hints: There are no thousands, hundreds, tens or ones.
questions.misconception: Writing 'five hundred million and three thousand' adds a thousands group that is not there.

questions.stem: Write 'four hundred and five thousand, two hundred' in figures.
questions.explanation: Four hundred and five thousand, two hundred = 405,200.
questions.misconception: Choosing 450,200 misreads 'four hundred and five' as 450.

questions.stem: Write 'six million, seventy thousand' in figures.
questions.misconception: Writing 6,700,000 places the 7 in the hundred-thousands instead of ten-thousands.

questions.stem: Write 'nine hundred and eighty-seven million, six hundred and fifty-four thousand, three hundred and twenty-one' in figures.
hints: Take each group in turn: millions = 987.
questions.misconception: Choosing 987,645,321 swaps the 5 and 4 in the thousands group.

hints: One billion is one thousand million.
questions.misconception: Choosing 100,000,000 writes one hundred million, not one billion.

questions.stem: Write 'eight thousand and nine' in figures.
hints: There are no hundreds or tens.
questions.misconception: Writing 8,900 places the 9 in the hundreds instead of the ones.

questions.stem: Write 'two hundred million, three hundred thousand' in figures.
questions.explanation: Two hundred million, three hundred thousand = 200,300,000.
questions.misconception: Writing 200,030,000 places the 3 in the ten-thousands instead of hundred-thousands.

questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 7 in 47,300?
hints: The 7 is in the thousands place.
questions.explanation: The 7 is in the thousands place, so its value is 7 × 1,000 = 7,000.
questions.misconception: Choosing 70,000 reads the 7 as if it were in the ten-thousands place.

hints: Break the number by place value.
questions.misconception: Choosing 300,000 + 50,000 + 40 misreads the 5 as fifty-thousand instead of five-thousand.

questions.stem: What is the place value of the digit 8 in 28,000,000?
hints: The 8 is in the second group from the left, in the millions place.
questions.explanation: In 28,000,000 the 8 is in the millions place.
questions.misconception: Choosing ten-millions confuses the 2 (ten-millions) with the 8 (millions).

hints: There is no thousands digit after 7? Actually 407,090 has 7 in thousands.
questions.misconception: Writing 400,000 + 700 + 90 places the 7 in the hundreds instead of thousands.
Choosing 'one hundred and twenty thousand' writes 120,000.
Choosing 'eighty thousand and eight' writes 80,008 instead of 80,080.
